statement: OpenAI's October 2026 manuscript claims a zero-free region Re(s)>7/8 for the Riemann zeta function and related L-functions; this is a partial result, not the Riemann Hypothesis.
source_title: The quasi-Riemann hypothesis — Lean formalization scope
source_version_or_commit: Public repository; exact revision should be pinned at ingestion
assumptions: The cited formalization scope is the source of the claim summary.
theorem_scope: Zero-free half-plane Re(s)>7/8; does not establish all non-trivial zeros have real part 1/2.
formalization_scope: Source documents a Lean formalization for the 7/8 zero-free statement; this record does not independently reproduce the build.
independent_review: A public community post reports a separate Lean re-check with caveats: https://community.openai.com/t/first-look-at-mathematics-manuscripts-from-an-internal-frontier-model-at-openai/1403886
counterevidence: A zero-free half-plane to the right of 7/8 is weaker than the Riemann Hypothesis and does not settle it.
unresolved_obligations: Pin the exact commit and independently reproduce the Lean build.
Audit the paper's proof and assumptions separately from kernel acceptance.
notes: Partial result only; do not label the Millennium Riemann Hypothesis solved.

statement: A manuscript claimed the rational Hodge conjecture for products of projective K3 surfaces; the authors subsequently withdrew it after identifying a proof gap.
source_title: Withdrawal notice: The rational Hodge conjecture for products of K3 surfaces
theorem_scope: Special family of products of K3 surfaces, not the full Hodge conjecture.
formalization_scope: Do not treat a formal artifact from the withdrawn manuscript as validating the withdrawn paper's mathematical claim.
counterevidence: The withdrawal notice states a sign error invalidates the stabilization-trace cancellation argument and leaves the claimed theorem unproved.
unresolved_obligations: Preserve the withdrawn version and notice.
Do not reinstate the claim without a repaired proof and independent review.
notes: Withdrawal concerns the proof; it does not prove the mathematical statement false.
